page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 12 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY processor cores operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 48.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1437.29 and a multi-core score of 23003.67. Memory performance tests show a read-only cached small block bandwidth of 1277.1 GB/sec, which drops to 102.76 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 36.67 GB/sec. In application-specific tests, the instance processes 21.93 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers a static web serving throughput of 16.94 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning, the system processes 1275.25 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 135M parameter model, dropping to 34.41 tokens per second on a 7B model.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.hfc6.6xlarge is its compute-heavy allocation ratio, which limits memory-intensive applications due to the 2.0 GB per vCPU constraint. The absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware further restricts its utility for massive database hosting or heavy deep learning training. However, its high clock speed and dedicated CPU allocation make it highly cost-efficient for compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints. It is well-suited for workloads such as software compilation, web serving, text and image processing, and moderate multi-threaded decompression tasks.
